`ExecutionContext` `dataclass`         *vllm.v1.metrics.perf.ExecutionContext*

Represents an execution context for a batch of requests.

This class aggregates statistics across multiple requests in a batch,
separately tracking prefill and decode phases.

Example) - Batch with one full prefill (2048 tokens) and one decode (1
token, 8192 context): ctx = ExecutionContext() ctx.add(2048, 2048,
is_prefill=True) ctx.add(1, 8192, is_prefill=False)

Methods: ~

- `add` -- Add a single request's statistics to this batch context.
- `decode_context_len_for_window` -- Sum of context_len for decode requests,
  clamped to sliding_window if set.
- `from_single_request` -- Create an ExecutionContext from a single request.
- `num_logits_tokens` -- Number of tokens that require logits computation
  (unembedding).
- `prefill_context_len_for_window` -- Sum of context_len for prefill
  requests, clamped to sliding_window if set.
- `total_num_tokens` -- Total number of tokens across all requests in the
  batch.
- `total_token_context_product` -- Total sum of (num_tokens * context_len)
  across all requests.

`MLAAttentionMetrics`               *vllm.v1.metrics.perf.MLAAttentionMetrics*

Bases: `ComponentMetrics`

Performance metrics for Multi-Latent Attention (MLA) layers.

MLA uses a compressed latent representation for KV cache: - KV cache stores
a single compressed vector of size (kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim) per
token per layer, instead of 2 * num_kv_heads * head_dim as in standard
MHA/GQA. - Q path uses optional low-rank compression: h -> q_lora_rank ->
num_heads * qk_head_dim - KV path: h -> (kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim),
then kv_lora_rank -> num_heads * (qk_nope_head_dim + v_head_dim)

Used by DeepSeek-V2, DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1, and similar models.

Methods: ~

- `component_type` -- Return the component registry key for MLA attention.
- `get_num_flops_breakdown` -- Calculate flops breakdown for MLA attention
  layers.
- `get_parser` -- Return the parser chain for MLAAttentionMetrics.
- `get_read_bytes_breakdown` -- Calculate read memory traffic for MLA
  attention layers.
- `get_write_bytes_breakdown` -- Calculate write memory traffic for MLA
  attention layers.

                     *vllm.v1.metrics.perf.MLAAttentionMetrics.component_type*
`component_type()` `classmethod`

Return the component registry key for MLA attention.

            *vllm.v1.metrics.perf.MLAAttentionMetrics.get_num_flops_breakdown*
`get_num_flops_breakdown(ctx, per_gpu=True)`

Calculate flops breakdown for MLA attention layers.

MLA projection structure: - Q path: h -> q_lora_rank -> num_heads *
qk_head_dim (or h -> num_heads * qk_head_dim if q_lora_rank is None) - KV
path: h -> (kv_lora_rank + qk_rope_head_dim), then kv_lora_rank -> num_heads
* (qk_nope_head_dim + v_head_dim) - Attention: Q @ K^T and attn @ V -
Output: num_heads * v_head_dim -> h

                         *vllm.v1.metrics.perf.MLAAttentionMetrics.get_parser*
`get_parser()` `classmethod`

Return the parser chain for MLAAttentionMetrics.

Parsers run in order: MLA detection guard, base model config, MLA-specific
config, quantization weight-size override.

           *vllm.v1.metrics.perf.MLAAttentionMetrics.get_read_bytes_breakdown*
`get_read_bytes_breakdown(ctx, per_gpu=True)`

Calculate read memory traffic for MLA attention layers.

          *vllm.v1.metrics.perf.MLAAttentionMetrics.get_write_bytes_breakdown*
`get_write_bytes_breakdown(ctx, per_gpu=True)`

Calculate write memory traffic for MLA attention layers.

`PerfMetricsProm`                       *vllm.v1.metrics.perf.PerfMetricsProm*

Record performance metrics in Prometheus.

Average TFLOPS (tera floating-point operations per second) can be calculated
using a PromQL query:

rate(vllm:estimated_flops_per_gpu_total[1m]) / 1e12

Average memory bandwidth in GB/s can be calculated using:

(rate(vllm:estimated_read_bytes_per_gpu_total[1m]) +
rate(vllm:estimated_write_bytes_per_gpu_total[1m])) / 1e9

Classes: ~

Functions: ~

  metrics.

`Counter` `dataclass`                         *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.Counter*

Bases: `Metric`

A monotonically increasing integer counter.

`Gauge` `dataclass`                             *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.Gauge*

Bases: `Metric`

A numerical value that can go up or down.

`Histogram` `dataclass`                     *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.Histogram*

Bases: `Metric`

Observations recorded in configurable buckets.

Buckets are represented by a dictionary. The key is the upper limit of the
bucket, and the value is the observed count in that bucket. A '+Inf' key
always exists.

The count property is the total count across all buckets, identical to the
count of the '+Inf' bucket.

The sum property is the total sum of all observed values.

`Metric` `dataclass`                           *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.Metric*

A base class for prometheus metrics.

Each metric may be associated with key=value labels, and in some cases a
single vLLM instance may have multiple metrics with the same name but
different sets of labels.

`Vector` `dataclass`                           *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.Vector*

Bases: `Metric`

An ordered array of integer counters.

This type - which doesn't exist in Prometheus - models one very specific
metric, vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_per_pos.

`get_metrics_snapshot()`         *vllm.v1.metrics.reader.get_metrics_snapshot*

An API for accessing in-memory Prometheus metrics.

  Example: ~

        for metric in llm.get_metrics(): ... if isinstance(metric, Counter):
        ... print(f"{metric} = {metric.value}") ... elif isinstance(metric,
        Gauge): ... print(f"{metric} = {metric.value}") ... elif
        isinstance(metric, Histogram): ... print(f"{metric}") ... print(f"
        sum = {metric.sum}") ... print(f" count = {metric.count}") ... for
        bucket_le, value in metrics.buckets.items(): ... print(f"
        {bucket_le} = {value}")

                              *vllm.v1.metrics.stats.RequestSpecDecodeMetrics*
`RequestSpecDecodeMetrics` `dataclass`

Per-output-sequence speculative-decoding statistics accumulator.

Accumulates, over one sequence's verify steps, a histogram of accepted
draft-token counts (`j`, draft-only) and the total number of proposed draft
tokens. When `detailed` is requested it also records the ordered per-step
accepted/proposed sequences (`summary` omits them). Tracked per engine
`Request` (one per sampled sequence, so `n > 1` yields one per child),
surfaced via `EngineCoreOutput` and the response
`metrics.speculative_decoding` for single-sequence requests (see `to_dict`).

  Fields: ~

  num_spec_tokens: Configured `num_speculative_tokens` (the max `k`); also
  the histogram's upper bound. histogram: Dense counts indexed by accepted
  draft tokens `j` (length `num_spec_tokens + 1`). num_draft_tokens: Total
  proposed draft tokens, including grammar-invalid ones. per_step_accepted:
  Ordered accepted-draft count per verify step (`detailed` only; empty
  otherwise). per_step_drafted: Ordered proposed-draft count per verify step
  (`detailed` only; empty otherwise). num_verified_tokens: Total draft
  tokens the target model ran a forward pass on. per_step_verified: Ordered
  verified-draft count per verify step (`detailed` only; empty otherwise).

Methods: ~

- `to_dict` -- Payload matching SpeculativeDecodingMetrics for the response.

`to_dict()`           *vllm.v1.metrics.stats.RequestSpecDecodeMetrics.to_dict*

Payload matching `SpeculativeDecodingMetrics` for the response.

`acceptance_histogram` is a dense list indexed by accepted draft count `j`
(length `num_spec_tokens + 1`). `mean_acceptance_length` includes the bonus
token (`j + 1`); `draft_acceptance_rate` is draft-only, full precision.
Per-step arrays are included only when populated (`detailed` level).

`MsgpackDecoder`                         *vllm.v1.serial_utils.MsgpackDecoder*

Decoder with custom torch tensor and numpy array serialization.

Note that unlike vanilla `msgspec` Decoders, this interface is generally not
thread-safe when encoding tensors / numpy arrays.

`oob_tensor_provider` must be used when an OOBTensorConsumer is used on the
encoder side.

`MsgpackEncoder`                         *vllm.v1.serial_utils.MsgpackEncoder*

Encoder with custom torch tensor and numpy array serialization.

Note that unlike vanilla `msgspec` Encoders, this interface is generally not
thread-safe when encoding tensors / numpy arrays.

By default, arrays below 256B are serialized inline Larger will get sent via
dedicated messages. Note that this is a per-tensor limit.

When a `oob_tensor_consumer` is provided, tensors (CUDA and CPU) will be
offered to it for out-of-band handling.

            *vllm.v1.structured_output.StructuredOutputManager._fill_bitmasks*
`_fill_bitmasks(batch)`

Fill one bitmask row per entry.

A row the grammar does not constrain allows every token except `masked_ids`,
the implicit reasoning ends masked while reasoning.

    *vllm.v1.structured_output.StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_bounds*
`_get_constraint_bounds(request, spec_tokens, spec_tokens_committed=False)`

Return the index into `spec_tokens` where tokens should start being
constrained by the grammar. Assumes `spec_tokens` are stripped of -1 padding
tokens. Returns `len(spec_tokens) + 1` if no token should be constrained
after accepting all `spec_tokens`. This is `constraint_start`;
`grammar_start` is one less if reasoning ends implicitly on a content token
(e.g. a tool-call start).

`spec_tokens_committed` is True if spec_tokens is already in
`request.all_token_ids`.

    *vllm.v1.structured_output.StructuredOutputManager._masked_reasoning_ends*
`_masked_reasoning_ends(request)`

Implicit reasoning-end tokens the grammar rejects as first content.

Such a token (e.g. a tool-call start) ends reasoning and is also the first
content token, so sampling one where the grammar cannot start with it would
make the output invalid. These stay masked while the request reasons. The
grammar does not advance before reasoning ends, so the set is fixed per
request.

             *vllm.v1.structured_output.StructuredOutputManager.accept_tokens*
`accept_tokens(request, new_token_ids)`

Advance grammar with accepted tokens. Returns False on rejection.

          *vllm.v1.structured_output.StructuredOutputManager.trim_spec_tokens*
`trim_spec_tokens(request, spec_tokens)`

Trim structured-output padding and grammar-invalid suffixes.

                                      *vllm.v1.token_buffer.extend_from_slice*
`extend_from_slice(dst, src, start, stop)`

`dst.extend(src[start:stop])`, copied without Python ints when both are
TokenBuffers.

                                  *vllm.v1.token_buffer.rfind_token_sequences*
`rfind_token_sequences(token_ids, markers, start=0, stop=None)`

Return `(index, k)` for the newest occurrence in `token_ids[start:stop]` of
any of the multi-token `markers`, `k` being its position in `markers` (the
first listed wins at the same index), or `(-1, -1)`.

Candidates are found with rfind_tokens on the markers' first tokens, so a
TokenBuffer is searched with numpy and only candidate positions are read.

                                           *vllm.v1.token_buffer.rfind_tokens*
`rfind_tokens(token_ids, targets, start=0, stop=None)`

Return the index of the last token in `token_ids[start:stop]` that is one of
`targets` (`None` entries, for absent tokens, are ignored), or -1.

An int32 buffer (a TokenBuffer) is searched with numpy, in chunks growing
back from `stop` so a recent match is found quickly, without creating a
Python int per token. Other sequences are scanned backwards in Python.

`token_slice(tokens, start, stop)`          *vllm.v1.token_buffer.token_slice*

`tokens[start:stop]`; for a TokenBuffer an int32 array, so that no Python
ints are made until it is read.

                        *vllm.v1.worker.dp_utils._post_process_cudagraph_mode*
`_post_process_cudagraph_mode(tensor)`

Synchronize cudagraph_mode across DP ranks by taking the minimum. If any
rank has NONE (0), all ranks use NONE. This ensures all ranks send
consistent values (all padded or all unpadded).

                               *vllm.v1.worker.dp_utils._synchronize_dp_ranks*
`_synchronize_dp_ranks(num_tokens_unpadded, num_tokens_padded,
    should_attempt_ubatching, cudagraph_mode, parallel_config)`

1. Decides if each DP rank is going to microbatch. Either all ranks run with
   microbatching or none of them do.
2. Determines the total number of tokens that each rank will run. When
   running microbatched or if cudagraph is enabled (synced across ranks),
   all ranks will be padded out so that they run with the same number of
   tokens.
3. Synchronizes cudagraph_mode across ranks by taking the minimum.

  *vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._generate_budgets*
`_generate_budgets(min_budget, max_budget, cap=None)` `staticmethod`

Generate token budgets from min_budget up to max_budget or cap.

Quarter-octave steps up to 1024 tokens, steps of 128 up to 2560, then
1/8-octave steps (rounded up to 128), so a replay pads at most ~25% below
1024, ~12% up to 2560 and ~9% above. Capture buffers are shared across
budgets (see `_capture_budget_graph`), so extra graphs cost no buffer
memory. Batches above the largest budget run eagerly.

*vllm.v1.worker.encoder_cudagraph.EncoderCudaGraphManager._share_prefix_compatible*
`_share_prefix_compatible(probe, shared)` `staticmethod`

View prefix-compatible probe buffers into the shared buffers.

For each probe buffer that is a row-prefix of its shared counterpart (same
trailing dims and dtype, no more rows), copy the probe contents into the
shared buffer and return the prefix view instead. Anything else, including
0-dim buffers (which hold per-budget values and save no memory when shared),
keeps its own per-budget allocation.

Extra capture axes beyond the token budget; empty to disable.

Optional per-buffer replay padding/copy logic. If absent for a key, the
manager slice-copies the replay buffer into the capture buffer and pads the
tail with the last value for cumulative keys (`cu_seqlens`,

whole capture buffer: budgets share buffers, so rows it leaves untouched may
hold another budget's data.

`ExtensibleKVCache`     *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.ExtensibleKVCache*

Growable backing allocation for the KV cache.

Reserves address space for `kv_cache_config.num_blocks` and commits a prefix
of blocks on demand. Blocks keep fixed offsets, so views over the
reservation and captured CUDA graphs stay valid as more are committed. The
allocation splits into segments holding num_blocks blocks each: one per
layer for block-compact layer-outermost layouts (sized by that layer's block
stride, possibly padded apart by `pad_kv_cache_segments`), one overall for
block-outermost. Host-resident tensors live outside it.

Methods: ~

- `allocate` -- Allocator hook for allocate_kv_cache; commits the minimum.
- `blocks_within` -- Most blocks whose physical footprint fits in num_bytes.
- `commit` -- Back the first num_blocks blocks; new blocks are zeroed.
- `committable_blocks` -- Blocks that can be committed now without eating
  into the headroom.
- `committed_kv_cache_tensors` -- Tensor placements matching committed_views
  for num_blocks.
- `committed_views` -- Per-layer views whose storage spans exactly the
  committed blocks.
- `physical_bytes_for` -- Bytes a commit of num_blocks maps, each segment
  rounded to granules.
- `recommit` -- Map fresh zeroed pages for the blocks committed before
  release.
- `record_transient_peak` -- Fold the allocated transient since peak
  tracking last restarted
- `release_physical` -- Drop physical pages for sleep; addresses and views
  stay valid.
- `set_torch_memory_limit` -- Cap what torch's caching allocator reserves on
  this device, or lift

Attributes: ~

- `min_committed_blocks` (int) -- The null block, plus one under
  block-outermost layouts, whose views
- `physical_bytes` (int) -- Physically mapped bytes, including granule
  rounding.

                 *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.ExtensibleKVCache.commit*
`commit(num_blocks, defragment=False, shrink=False)`

Back the first num_blocks blocks; new blocks are zeroed.

Grow-only unless shrink is set, which remaps a smaller prefix and discards
contents. defragment remaps each segment as one driver allocation
(discarding contents): UCX cannot RDMA a range spanning several allocations.

     *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.ExtensibleKVCache.committable_blocks*
`committable_blocks()`

Blocks that can be committed now without eating into the headroom.

Bounds what warmup may commit: free memory plus the committed prefix, less
the sizing margin and the larger of reserved_headroom_bytes and a share of
the headroom, never below what is already committed nor above the capacity.

*vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.ExtensibleKVCache.committed_kv_cache_tensors*
`committed_kv_cache_tensors(kv_cache_config, layout, num_blocks)`

Tensor placements matching committed_views for num_blocks.

size is the committed total, as every device tensor describes the one
allocation; host-resident tensors are unchanged. Under block-outermost
layouts the committed blocks are one prefix of it, so the capacity
placements still hold. Under layer-outermost layouts each layer's view has
its own storage over its committed prefix: describe it as a one-layer tensor
placed at the start of that storage.

        *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.ExtensibleKVCache.committed_views*
`committed_views(kv_cache_config, layout, kernel_block_sizes=None)`

Per-layer views whose storage spans exactly the committed blocks.

`kv_cache_config.num_blocks` must equal the committed count. Connectors
derive extents from `untyped_storage().nbytes()`, so they must not see the
reservation. Host-resident layers are omitted. None for layouts whose layers
span several segments.

     *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.ExtensibleKVCache.physical_bytes_for*
`physical_bytes_for(num_blocks)`

Bytes a commit of num_blocks maps, each segment rounded to granules.

                          *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.extend_kv_cache*
`extend_kv_cache(runner, kv_cache_config, num_blocks)`

Commit the final size once post-warmup memory is known.

             *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.kv_cache_export_handle_types*

          *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.kv_cache_lent_for_weight_update*
`kv_cache_lent_for_weight_update(kv_cache, model, *, reclaimable,
    fail_if_short)`

Make room for a layerwise weight update of model within the context.

Only an extensible KV cache (kv_cache, None for a standard one) leaves the
free memory short, since it keeps free just the transients warmup measured.
When short, release the cache's physical memory for the context if it holds
nothing to keep (reclaimable); else fail before any weight changes, when not
even the largest layer fits and fail_if_short, or warn. Torch's memory cap
is lifted for the context.

                  *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.measure_kv_cache_blocks*
`measure_kv_cache_blocks(kv_cache, vllm_config, device, *, init_free_memory,
    requested_memory)`

Size an extensible KV cache from the memory free after warmup.

Keeps free the larger of reserved_headroom_bytes (the profiled or warmup
allocated peak) and torch_reserve_growth_bytes. Torch's cache is emptied
first: its blocks may not fit the large workspaces the first real steps
allocate. Then caps torch's caching allocator to leave
KV_CACHE_NON_TORCH_RESERVE_BYTES free for allocations outside it.

                   *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.measure_kv_cache_bytes*
`measure_kv_cache_bytes(*, init_free_memory, free_memory, committed_bytes,
    requested_memory, transient_peak_bytes=0, torch_reserve_growth_bytes=0,
    margin_floor_bytes=KV_CACHE_MARGIN_FLOOR_BYTES,
    margin_fraction=KV_CACHE_MARGIN_FRACTION)`

Bytes the KV cache may occupy given the memory measured after warmup.

Everything resident except the committed KV prefix is needed by the engine;
the cache gets the rest of the budget, capped by the device headroom (free
memory plus the committed prefix) less a margin of
`max(margin_floor_bytes, margin_fraction * transient_peak_bytes)`. The
larger of transient_peak_bytes and torch_reserve_growth_bytes is then kept
free in full. The margin guards physical memory, so it never reduces an
explicit budget that already leaves that much free.

                *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.num_committable_kv_blocks*
`num_committable_kv_blocks(runner)`

Blocks warmup may address: all of them, or, for an extensible cache, the
count agreed across ranks so that every rank warms up the same shapes.

                    *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.pad_kv_cache_segments*
`pad_kv_cache_segments(kv_cache_config, layout, granule, *,
    registers_memory=False)`

Start every layer's region on a granule.

Committing the null block then backs each layer's first granule, which TMA
gathers with out-of-bounds indices touch beyond the rows they address. It
also lets a defragmenting commit of any block count back each segment with
one physical chunk, as RDMA registration (registers_memory) requires.

Only address space grows: commits already map whole granules per segment.
Block-outermost layouts (one segment at offset 0, see `allocate`) are
returned as is, and so are other layouts that are not block-compact, unless
registers_memory.

                *vllm.v1.worker.extensible_kv_cache.registers_kv_cache_memory*
`registers_kv_cache_memory(vllm_config)`

Whether a KV connector registers the committed KV cache for RDMA, which
needs each segment backed by one physical chunk.

   *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.attn_utils.get_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_eligible_layers*
`get_kv_sharing_fast_prefill_eligible_layers(vllm_config,
    draft_layer_names=None)`

Trailing run of KV-sharing layers, eligible for fast prefill.

In You Only Cache Once (https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.05254) or other similar
KV sharing setups, only the layers that generate KV caches are involved in
the prefill phase, enabling prefill to early exit. Layers are registered in
execution order, so the eligible layers are the contiguous suffix of
KV-sharing layers.

Speculator draft layers register after the target model's layers (and may
themselves share KV), so they are excluded from the walk.

   *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.attn_utils.get_query_lens_mismatch_unsupported_backend*
`get_query_lens_mismatch_unsupported_backend(attn_groups,
    checked_layer_names=None)`

Name the first backend needing the CPU query lengths to be exact, if any.

The attention selector already excludes these when adaptive verification is
enabled, but models that hard-wire their backend never consult it. See
AttentionBackend.supports_device_cpu_query_lens_mismatch().

      *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.attn_utils.get_varlen_cudagraph_unsupported_backend*
`get_varlen_cudagraph_unsupported_backend(attn_groups, vllm_config,
    max_query_len, checked_layer_names=None)`

Name the first backend whose FULL cudagraphs cannot replay decode batches of
1 to max_query_len tokens per request, with its bound, if any.

ALWAYS builders replay any batch; the others need a bound of at least
max_query_len. See
AttentionMetadataBuilder.get_varlen_cudagraph_max_query_len().

                                              *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.block_table*

Classes: ~

- `BlockTables` --

Functions: ~

- `make_slot_mappings` -- Allocate a [num_groups, num_tokens] int64
  slot-mapping buffer.

`BlockTables`                     *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.block_table.BlockTables*

Methods: ~

- `gather_block_tables` -- Gather the batch's block-table rows into the
  forward-pass tables.

              *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.block_table.BlockTables.gather_block_tables*
`gather_block_tables(idx_mapping, num_reqs_padded, out=None, out_ptrs=None,
    num_computed_tokens=None)`

Gather the batch's block-table rows into the forward-pass tables.

When num_computed_tokens ([max_num_reqs], indexed like the block tables) is
given, sliding-window groups get every entry wholly below the window of the
request's first scheduled token replaced by the null block. Those blocks may
already have been freed by the sliding-window manager and reused, while
attention kernels can still load them as part of a KV tile that straddles
the window start: masked-out NaN in such a tile propagates into the output.

                           *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.block_table.make_slot_mappings*
`make_slot_mappings(num_groups, num_tokens, device)`

Allocate a [num_groups, num_tokens] int64 slot-mapping buffer.

Each group's row is handed to attention as its own tensor, and some kernels
assume an aligned base address (DeepSeek-V4's CuTe DSL compressor requires
64 bytes). Pad the row stride so every row starts 128-byte aligned whatever
num_tokens is.

`CudaGraphManager`       *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils.CudaGraphManager*

Captures and dispatches the CUDA graphs of one runner.

Uniform decode batches of query length `q` take graphs of `n` requests, for
each `q` in `decode_query_lens` and `n` in `decode_request_sizes` (default
`decode_cudagraph_capture_request_sizes`) up to the requests `q` maps to.
With `varlen_decode` (adaptive verification) they take token-keyed graphs of
`get_varlen_decode_cudagraph_token_sizes` instead. Other batches, and all
batches when one routine runs every batch, take token-keyed graphs of
`prefill_cudagraph_capture_token_sizes`.

Methods: ~

- `capture` -- Capture CUDA graphs.
- `captured_token_counts` -- Sorted token counts with a captured graph,
  ignoring LoRA variants.
- `dispatch` -- Find the graph to run a batch with, else an eager
  descriptor.
- `release_graphs` -- Drop the captured graphs so a later capture() can
  refill them.
- `run_fullgraph` -- Replay a captured FULL cudagraph.

*vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils.CudaGraphManager._build_lora_dispatch_map*
`_build_lora_dispatch_map()`

Precompute actual num_active_loras -> effective captured case.

Mirrors the num_tokens candidate expansion in `_init_candidates`: every
possible active-LoRA count is mapped ahead of time to the smallest captured
case that can serve it, so `dispatch` is a plain dict lookup instead of a
per-call bisect.

    max_query_len=None, num_ubatches=1)`

Find the graph to run a batch with, else an eager descriptor.

A uniform decode batch takes the smallest decode graph of its query length
that covers `num_tokens`, which may be padded (e.g. to the DP maximum), if
that graph holds its requests. Other batches, and decode batches no decode
graph takes, take the smallest compatible token-keyed graph.

          *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils.CudaGraphManager.release_graphs*
`release_graphs()`

Drop the captured graphs so a later capture() can refill them.

Elastic EP reallocates the MoE workspace when it grows, which leaves every
captured graph holding a stale data pointer. `_capture_descs` is kept, so
`needs_capture()` still reports the work to redo.

     *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils._init_minimal_kv_cache_for_profiling*

                *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils._teardown_profiling_state*
`_teardown_profiling_state(runner)`

                   *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils.has_compiled_submodule*
`has_compiled_submodule(model)`

Whether any submodule is an active @support_torch_compile module.

                 *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.cudagraph_utils.profile_cudagraph_memory*
`profile_cudagraph_memory(runner)`

Estimate the GPU memory needed for CUDA graph capture.

Called during memory profiling, before the real KV cache is allocated, so
that `Worker.determine_available_memory` can reserve headroom for graph
capture. Bootstraps a minimal KV cache, runs `capture_model()` once, then
releases everything so the real init/capture path starts clean.

FULL graphs bake in KV cache pointers, so only the largest few are captured
(into a throwaway pool) and their total cost is extrapolated. PIECEWISE,
encoder and speculator graphs are measured in full. All profiling captures
are discarded afterwards: replaying graphs recorded against the throwaway
profiling state is unsafe (e.g. inductor graph partition reclaims the
storages of earlier cudagraph recordings once the real capture records new
ones, leading to use-after-free crashes).

`DPSyncState` `dataclass`            *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.dp_utils.DPSyncState*

What a `dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp` call agreed across DP ranks.

Every field is identical on every rank, so callers can branch on them
without disagreeing about whether to run a collective. Never add a per-rank
value here.

                         *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.dp_utils.dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp*
`dispatch_cg_and_sync_dp(cudagraph_manager, num_reqs, num_tokens,
    uniform_token_count, dp_size, dp_rank, max_query_len=None, need_eager=False,
    num_active_loras=0, parallel_config=None, allow_ubatching=False,
    uniform_decode=False, allow_skip_drafts=False, dp_sync_state=None)`

Pick a cudagraph descriptor for this batch, agreeing it across DP ranks.

Runs a collective when dp_size > 1 so every rank dispatches to the same
shape. Pass `dp_sync_state` from a dispatch already made over this same
batch (a drafter's prefill runs the target's batch shape) to reuse that
agreement instead, with no collective.

Parameters: ~

- `cudagraph_manager` (CudaGraphManager | None) -- Manager to dispatch
  against. May be None only when need_eager is True (profile run).
- `num_reqs` (int) -- Requests in this rank's batch.
- `num_tokens` (int) -- Tokens in this rank's batch, already padded by the
  caller.
- `uniform_token_count` (int | None) -- Per-request token count if this
  rank's batch is a uniform decode, else None.
  dp_sync_state.uniform_token_count takes its place when a sync is reused,
  since that one is agreed across ranks.
- `dp_size` (int) -- Data-parallel world size. 1 skips all cross-rank work.
- `dp_rank` (int) -- This rank's index in the DP group.
- `max_query_len` (int | None, default: None ) -- Upper bound on per-request
  query length, for selecting varlen decode graphs. None, as for a batch
  that is not decode-graph eligible, keeps the batch out of graphs that
  constrain it. Reusing a sync replaces this with
  dp_sync_state.max_query_len, including when it is None.
- `need_eager` (bool, default: False ) -- Force CUDAGraphMode.NONE instead
  of dispatching.
- `num_active_loras` (int, default: 0 ) -- Active LoRA count for this rank.
  Does not need cross-rank agreement; it never changes a bucket's token
  count.
- `parallel_config` (ParallelConfig | None, default: None ) -- Only needed
  for FT coordination and to decide whether to microbatch, so callers that
  do neither can leave it out.
- `allow_ubatching` (bool, default: False ) -- Whether this rank's batch may
  be split into microbatches. Agreed across ranks before it takes effect.
- `uniform_decode` (bool, default: False ) -- Whether this rank's batch is a
  uniform decode, used to pick the microbatching split.
- `allow_skip_drafts` (bool, default: False ) -- Whether this rank allows
  skipping drafts, because none of its requests can use this step's drafts.
  Agreed across ranks (all must allow it) into DPSyncState.skip_drafts.
- `dp_sync_state` (DPSyncState | None, default: None ) -- Agreement from a
  prior dispatch over this same batch, to reuse. Must come from a batch with
  this same padded num_tokens and the same uniform_token_count; num_reqs may
  differ, as neither depends on it. Passing a sync from a different batch is
  a caller error and trips an assert.

Returns: ~

- `BatchExecutionDescriptor` -- (batch_desc, sync), where sync is this
  batch's agreement for a later
- `DPSyncState | None` -- dispatch to reuse. It is None when dp_size is 1 or
  no rank has work.

                   *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.dp_utils.sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding*
`sync_cudagraph_and_dp_padding(cudagraph_manager, desired_batch_desc,
    num_tokens, num_reqs, uniform_token_count, dp_size, dp_rank,
    max_query_len=None, num_active_loras=0, parallel_config=None,
    allow_ubatching=False, uniform_decode=False, allow_skip_drafts=False)`

Coordinates the batch descriptor and DP padding across all ranks.

Returns (synced_batch_desc, sync). `sync` is None when no rank has work.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                             *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_runner*

NOTE: Coding style guide for this file: This model runner is shared by all
models: text and multimodal, generative and embedding, public and private.
As a result, this file must only contain code that is common to every model.
Model-specific behavior belongs in the appropriate model-specific files.

In other words: * Be paranoid about changing this file. It should remain
stable. * Be even more paranoid about adding new lines. It should remain
minimal.

Even for shared features (for example, different parallelism modes), keep
the complexity out of this path. The less common the feature, the more it
should be hidden. Prefer utility functions defined elsewhere and call them
from here, instead of embedding feature-specific logic directly.

`PCPManager`                       *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.pcp_manager.PCPManager*

MRV2 PC batch manager.

The model runner keeps the global scheduled batch. This manager rewrites
only the per-step InputBatch into rank-local DualChunkSwap rows and keeps
the global-batch view private to restore to the global batch shape before
sampling/postprocess.

  every PCP rank, to
- `prepare_inputs_for_capture_or_profile` -- Stage a capture or dummy batch

                 *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.pcp_manager.PCPManager._iter_rank_chunks*
`_iter_rank_chunks(rank, num_scheduled_tokens, is_prefilling)`

Yield `(request index, query offset, length)` for one PCP rank.

PCP=4 partitions each prefill into eight chunks:

>text
    full:  | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 |
    rank 0:  0                           7
    rank 1:      1                   6
    rank 2:          2           5
    rank 3:              3   4
<
Decodes, and prefills too short to fill all eight, are replicated instead.

                 *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.pcp_manager.PCPManager._reorder_segments*
`_reorder_segments(segments, is_prefilling)` `staticmethod`

Order this rank's rows decodes-first, then prefills, canonically.

`PPHandler`                            *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.pp_utils.PPHandler*

Runs the PP sampled-token broadcast/recv on a side stream so the default
stream isn't gated by the matching peer call. Step T's recv is consumed at
step T+pp_size via `get_prev_sampled_outputs`.

Uses a dedicated NCCL communicator (sibling of the PP `device_group`) for
the broadcast so it does not serialize on the wire with the inter-stage
hidden-state p2p send/recv ops.

Methods: ~

- `add_positions_buffer` -- Add the relayed positions to the persistent
  intermediate tensors,
- `add_upstream_aux_hidden_states` -- Turn the last stage's model output,
  which carries only the aux hidden
- `broadcast_drafts` -- Broadcast draft proposals so non-last ranks can
  embed real token ids.
- `get_prev_sampled_outputs` -- Consume the entry from pp_size steps ago and
  wait for its recv event,
- `receive` -- Returns True iff sampled tokens need to be gathered from all
- `receive_positions` -- Overwrite the locally prepared positions with the
  first stage's.
- `relay_aux_hidden_states` -- Forward earlier stages' aux hidden states
  next to this stage's.
- `send_positions` -- Add this step's positions to the tensors sent to the
  next stage.

                  *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.pp_utils.PPHandler.add_positions_buffer*
`add_positions_buffer(intermediate_tensors, max_num_tokens, num_dims)`

Add the relayed positions to the persistent intermediate tensors, which

                    *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.batch_shard.BatchShardMetadata*
`BatchShardMetadata` `dataclass`

Collective layout for one sampling step.

Requests (and their logits) are owner-sorted: all requests owned by rank 0
first, then rank 1, etc. Within an owner, batch order is preserved (stable
sort). Every field is a pure function of the replicated idx_mapping and
cu_num_logits, so all ranks build identical plans without communication ---
which relies on request slots (idx_mapping) being assigned identically on
every rank (see finish_requests in the model runner).

`BatchSharder`            *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.batch_shard.BatchSharder*

  sampler inputs.

Owner-sort the batch and build this rank's local sampler inputs.

Argmax of logits under Gumbel-max sampling, or plain argmax at temp 0.

`keys` indexes the noise, so the same token draws the same noise wherever it
appears; `pos` and `seed` place the draw in the request's stream, which is
what lets a draft and its verification agree.

                                  *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor*

Custom logits processors for the V2 model runner.

Kept import-light: the frontend process imports this package to validate
per-request params, so nothing here may pull in model-runner side modules
(torch, triton, worker state) at import time.

Modules: ~

- `interface` -- V2 logits processor interface.
- `loader` -- Loading of custom logits processor classes for the V2 model
  runner.

Classes: ~

- `LogitsContext` -- The current step's batch layout, passed to every
  apply() call.
- `LogitsProcRequestState` -- State associated with active requests, shared
  with logits processors.
- `LogitsProcessor` -- Custom logits processor for Model Runner V2.

Functions: ~

- `build_custom_logits_processors` -- Load and instantiate custom logits
  processors, entrypoint plugins first.
- `build_custom_logits_processors_params_validator` -- Load custom processor
  classes once and return a params validator.

                    *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.LogitsContext*
`LogitsContext` `dataclass`

The current step's batch layout, passed to every `apply()` call.

A row is a logits row, not a request: rows are reordered every step, and
under speculative decoding a request owns one row per draft token. Committed
tokens live in `req_states.all_token_ids` (valid up to `total_len`); this
step's draft tokens are only in `input_ids`.

           *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.LogitsProcRequestState*
`LogitsProcRequestState` `dataclass`

State associated with active requests, shared with logits processors.

Wraps the model runner's per-slot buffers, which are mutated in place, so
reads always see current values. Processors must treat every field as
read-only.

`LogitsProcessor` *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.LogitsProcessor*

Bases: `ABC`

Custom logits processor for Model Runner V2.

Per-request state is keyed by the request slot index; slots are recycled
through a free list, so per-slot state must be fully (re)initialized in
`add_request()`.

`apply()` runs after the built-in bias, penalty, bad-words and grammar
stages and before temperature, min_p and top-k/top-p, so it sees unscaled
logits and must not re-inflate grammar-masked tokens. Thinking-budget
forcing runs after `apply()` and wins over its edits for requests whose
budget is exhausted.

State that is constant for a request belongs in `__init__()` or
`add_request()`; `apply()` receives only what changes per step.

Methods: ~

- `__init__` -- Capture what stays constant for the processor's lifetime.
- `add_request` -- Initialize per-slot state for a request entering the
  batch.
- `apply` -- Modify logits in place or return a new tensor. In-place
  modification
- `apply_staged_writes` -- Flush any host-side writes staged by
  add_request() to the device.
- `validate_params` -- Raise ValueError for invalid per-request arguments.

         *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.LogitsProcessor.__init__*
`__init__(vllm_config, req_states)`

Capture what stays constant for the processor's lifetime.

`req_states` exposes the on-device token history and batch constants a
processor may read. Treat it as read-only.

      *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.LogitsProcessor.add_request*
`add_request(req_idx, sampling_params)`

Initialize per-slot state for a request entering the batch.

The slot may hold a previous occupant's state; overwrite or neutralize all
of it here.

Returns whether this processor modifies logits for the request.

            *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.LogitsProcessor.apply*
`apply(logits, ctx)` `abstractmethod`

Modify logits in place or return a new tensor. In-place modification is
preferred for efficiency.

`apply()` is called once for the whole batch, including rows of requests
this processor declined in `add_request()`, so filter rows via
`ctx.expanded_idx_mapping`.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                        *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.interface*

V2 logits processor interface.

Import-light by design: custom processor classes are also loaded in the
frontend process (to validate per-request params), so this module must not
pull in model-runner side modules (torch, triton, worker state) at import
time. Heavy imports live under TYPE_CHECKING; annotations are deferred.

Classes: ~

- `LogitsContext` -- The current step's batch layout, passed to every
  apply() call.
- `LogitsProcRequestState` -- State associated with active requests, shared
  with logits processors.
- `LogitsProcessor` -- Custom logits processor for Model Runner V2.

          *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.interface.LogitsContext*
`LogitsContext` `dataclass`

The current step's batch layout, passed to every `apply()` call.

A row is a logits row, not a request: rows are reordered every step, and
under speculative decoding a request owns one row per draft token. Committed
tokens live in `req_states.all_token_ids` (valid up to `total_len`); this
step's draft tokens are only in `input_ids`.

 *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.interface.LogitsProcRequestState*
`LogitsProcRequestState` `dataclass`

State associated with active requests, shared with logits processors.

Wraps the model runner's per-slot buffers, which are mutated in place, so
reads always see current values. Processors must treat every field as
read-only.

        *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logits_processor.interface.LogitsProcessor*
`LogitsProcessor`

Bases: `ABC`

Custom logits processor for Model Runner V2.

Per-request state is keyed by the request slot index; slots are recycled
through a free list, so per-slot state must be fully (re)initialized in
`add_request()`.

`apply()` runs after the built-in bias, penalty, bad-words and grammar
stages and before temperature, min_p and top-k/top-p, so it sees unscaled
logits and must not re-inflate grammar-masked tokens. Thinking-budget
forcing runs after `apply()` and wins over its edits for requests whose
budget is exhausted.

State that is constant for a request belongs in `__init__()` or
`add_request()`; `apply()` receives only what changes per step.

Methods: ~

- `__init__` -- Capture what stays constant for the processor's lifetime.
- `add_request` -- Initialize per-slot state for a request entering the
  batch.
- `apply` -- Modify logits in place or return a new tensor. In-place
  modification
- `apply_staged_writes` -- Flush any host-side writes staged by
  add_request() to the device.
- `validate_params` -- Raise ValueError for invalid per-request arguments.

`TraceReplayState`   *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.trace_replay.TraceReplayState*

Per-request state for inference trace-replay.

When a request carries `SamplingParams.trace_decode_token_ids`, the sampler
overwrites the sampled token at each decode step with the predetermined
trace token, while real logprobs and ranks are still computed from the
unmodified logit distribution. The replay step for a request is derived
entirely from GPU state (`total_len - prompt_len`), so no CPU
synchronization or async placeholder handling is needed.

              *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.watermark.draft_philox_gumbel_sample*
`draft_philox_gumbel_sample(logits, contexts, key, *, num_steps,

Sample `num_steps` draft steps flattened as (request, step), in step order.

Bit-exact with sampling each step by `DraftWatermarker.sample`, but with two
kernel launches per step: the Philox block argmax (with the temperature
divide and the logits cache write), then a per-row kernel that picks the
token, shifts `contexts` and builds the next step's skip mask. Padding rows
(index -1) read temperature 0 and are never watermarked, so they may differ.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                         *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.acceptance_estimator*

Classes: ~

- `OnlineAcceptanceEstimator` -- Predicts per-position acceptance, and
  calibrates itself while serving.

*vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.acceptance_estimator.OnlineAcceptanceEstimator*
`OnlineAcceptanceEstimator`

Predicts per-position acceptance, and calibrates itself while serving.

Lifecycle per step, driven by `DraftModelSpeculator`:

1. `step` folds the previous step's drafts, now graded by the target, into
   the IRLS accumulators, and periodically solves for new coefficients,
   independently but identically on every rank.
2. `predict` runs inside the captured draft graph, turning this step's draft
   logits into acceptance probabilities for adaptive verification.

Trimming starts immediately: survival is a running product of sigmoids, so
it decreases with draft position whatever the coefficients are, and an
unfitted estimator degrades to uniform-depth truncation rather than to
anything harmful.

Methods: ~

- `warmup` -- Drop warmup statistics and compile the refit kernel. A refit
  on

*vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.acceptance_estimator.OnlineAcceptanceEstimator.warmup*
`warmup()`

Drop warmup statistics and compile the refit kernel. A refit on zeroed
statistics leaves the coefficients unchanged.

    *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.acceptance_estimator._max_and_excl_sumexp*
`_max_and_excl_sumexp(logits)`

Block max, and its sumexp with one copy of that max left out.

The excluding sum is what keeps the feature accurate. Forming the full sum
and subtracting the max's own e^(m-m) = 1 term afterwards is catastrophic
cancellation: the complement mass is the whole quantity of interest, and it
is gone as soon as it falls below an fp32 ulp of 1.0 (~6e-8), which a
confident drafter reaches routinely.

    *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.adaptive_verification.AdmittedDraftCounts*
`AdmittedDraftCounts`

*vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.adaptive_verification.assign_draft_token_budget*
`assign_draft_token_budget(confidence_probs, idx_mapping, capacities,
    draft_budget, survival)`

Admit the globally best `draft_budget` draft slots, in place.

Every (request, step) slot is scored by its survival probability, the
running product of that request's per-position confidences, and the highest
scores win. Survival only decreases along a request, so the winners are
always a prefix of each request's steps and only per-request counts are
needed.

`capacities` enters holding each request's scheduled draft count (which
bounds its eligible slots) and leaves holding the admitted count. The caller
only calls this when `draft_budget < capacities.sum()`, so every winner is a
real draft slot. `survival` is int32 scratch with room for
`num_reqs * num_steps` slots.

*vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.adaptive_verification.build_cost_tables_from_curves*
`build_cost_tables_from_curves(draft_curve, verify_curve, max_num_reqs,
    max_batch_tokens, cudagraph_limit=0)`

Build cost tables: graph-padded below the capture limit, smooth above.

Parameters: ~

- `draft_curve` (list[tuple[int, float]]) -- (size, cost) samples for the
  draft model.
- `verify_curve` (list[tuple[int, float]]) -- (size, cost) samples for the
  verify model.
- `max_num_reqs` (int) -- Largest request count to build a table for.
- `max_batch_tokens` (int) -- Largest token count to build a table for.
- `cudagraph_limit` (int, default: 0 ) -- Largest cudagraph-captured size.
  At or below it, execution pads up to the next captured size, so cost is a
  step function. Above it there is no padding, so cost is continuous.

*vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.adaptive_verification.resolve_adaptive_cudagraph_mode*
`resolve_adaptive_cudagraph_mode(mode, *, piecewise_capture_available)`

                                 *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.draft_logits*

                *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.draft_logits.DraftLogitsCache*
`DraftLogitsCache`

Pre-temperature draft logits, cached by a draft step for the next
verification.

A replicated cache holds every request on every TP rank, at row
req_state_idx.

A sharded cache (batch-sharded sampling) holds on each TP rank only the
requests that rank verifies. Every draft step gives the request at batch
position i to rank i % tp, at row i // tp of its cache, so no rank caches
more than cdiv(num_reqs, tp) requests however the request slots are spread.

Rows are reused every step. A request that the scheduler skips for a step
keeps its drafts, but its row may since have been given to another request.
`inverse_row_mapping` detects this, and `stale_drafts` marks those drafts
invalid, so verification rejects them and samples from the target.

Methods: ~

- `assign` -- Give a sharded cache's rows out by batch position. Call after
- `owners_of` -- The TP rank that verifies each of a batch's requests: the
  rank that
- `stale_drafts` -- Mark the drafts whose draft logits were overwritten
  since drafting.

         *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.draft_logits.DraftLogitsCache.assign*
`assign(idx_mapping, idx_mapping_np)`

Give a sharded cache's rows out by batch position. Call after verification
and before the draft step writes the draft logits.

      *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.draft_logits.DraftLogitsCache.owners_of*
`owners_of(idx_mapping_np)`

The TP rank that verifies each of a batch's requests: the rank that cached
its draft logits, or for a replicated cache, round-robin over batch
positions.

Returns: ~

- `ndarray` -- [num_reqs] each request's owner, and the [max_num_reqs]
  device owner
- `Tensor | None` -- table, or None for a replicated cache.

   *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.draft_logits.DraftLogitsCache.stale_drafts*
`stale_drafts(input_batch)`

Mark the drafts whose draft logits were overwritten since drafting. Only
valid for requests this rank owns.

Returns: ~

- `Tensor | None` -- [num_logits] True for each stale draft, or None for a
  replicated
- `Tensor | None` -- cache, whose rows are never reused.

                *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.draft_logits.draft_logits_row*
`draft_logits_row(req_state_idx, row_mapping_ptr)`

Row of a request in this rank's draft logits cache, or -1 if no row.

`row_mapping_ptr` is None for a replicated cache, which is indexed by

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                          *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.fly*

Entropy-gated deferred verification for FLy speculative decoding.

FLy defers a high-entropy rejection when the next `W` draft tokens would be
accepted natively. The rejection kernel applies these decisions.

Functions: ~

- `compute_fly_entropy` -- Normalized top-k entropy in [0, 1].

                      *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.fly.compute_fly_entropy*
`compute_fly_entropy(values, entropy_top_k, *, from_logits=False)`

Normalized top-k entropy in `[0, 1]`.

Takes the largest `k` target scores, renormalizes them into a distribution
over those `k` candidates only, then divides the Shannon entropy by `log(k)`
so that `fly_entropy_threshold` keeps the same meaning for every
`fly_entropy_top_k`.

`BaseSpeculator`    *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.speculator.BaseSpeculator*

Bases: `ABC`

Base class for V2 model runner speculators.

This is also the interface for custom speculators, named by the
`speculator_class` of their registered `SpeculatorConfig` (see
`register_speculative_method`). Speculators that run a draft model should
subclass `DraftModelSpeculator` (or `TargetDependentARSpeculator` if
drafting consumes target model state), which the model runner loads and
allocates draft KV cache for.

Methods: ~

- `on_requests_finished` -- Requests finished (not preempted), before their
  request-state slots
- `prepare_watermarking` -- Prepare draft-side watermarking before propose.
  No-op by default.
- `reset_state` -- Forget anything learned across requests, called after the
  warmup
- `shutdown` -- Called when the model runner shuts down. Detaches a draft
  model's
- `update_max_model_len` -- Apply a reduced max_model_len. Auto-fit can call
  this after capture,

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                            *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.speculator_config*

Per-speculator configuration.

Each speculator has a `SpeculatorConfig` subclass, in a `config.py` next to
its V2 model runner implementation, which sets up `SpeculativeConfig` for
it, describes its behavior to code outside the speculator (queried through
`SpeculativeConfig.speculator_config` rather than by method name), and names
its implementation class. Config modules must not import the speculators, as
they're used in every process. Custom speculators are registered with
`register_speculative_method`.

Classes: ~

- `DraftModelSpeculatorConfig` -- A speculator whose draft model is loaded
  from the model checkpoint.
- `SpeculatorConfig` -- Configuration of a kind of speculator.

Functions: ~

- `get_custom_speculator_config_class` -- The config of a registered custom
  speculative method, or None.
- `get_method_config_class` -- Select method and target-family configuration
  before loading the draft.
- `get_speculator_config_class` -- The config class for a set-up spec
  config.
- `register_speculative_method` -- Register a custom speculative method,
  used with method=name.
- `registered_speculative_methods` -- The names of the registered custom
  speculative methods.

                                             *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils*

Microbatching (DBO) helpers for the V2 GPU model runner.

Classes: ~

`UBatchRunner`                  *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils.UBatchRunner*

Runs the model on two or more microbatches that overlap each other.

Each microbatch gets a thread and its own forward context. Only one thread
holds the GPU at a time; they hand off to each other at the communication
points inside the model (see `vllm.v1.worker.ubatching`), so one
microbatch's expert all-to-all overlaps the other's compute.

Methods: ~

- `abort_pending_run` -- Release and join parked threads after a failed
  capture.
- `begin_capturable_run` -- Start microbatch threads and return a callback
  to run and join them.
- `prepare` -- Split the batch into the microbatches the step will run on.

         *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils.UBatchRunner._make_forward_contexts*
`_make_forward_contexts(ubatch_slices, attn_metadata,
    slot_mappings_by_layer, is_padding)`

Build one forward context per microbatch.

The expert all-to-all runs once per microbatch, so each context's DP
metadata carries that microbatch's token count. Microbatching pads every DP
rank alike, so each rank can assume that count for the others too.

              *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils.UBatchRunner.abort_pending_run*
`abort_pending_run()`

Release and join parked threads after a failed capture.

           *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils.UBatchRunner.begin_capturable_run*
`begin_capturable_run(model, model_inputs, ubatch_state, for_capture=False)`

Start microbatch threads and return a callback to run and join them.

For capture, start threads outside the graph and call the callback inside.
`for_capture` selects the capture stream and initializes cuBLAS workspaces
before capture.

Call the callback exactly once on this thread, or call `abort_pending_run`
on failure to release parked threads.

                        *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils.UBatchRunner.prepare*
`prepare(input_batch, block_tables, slot_mappings, batch_desc,
    dp_sync_state=None, for_capture=False)`

Split the batch into the microbatches the step will run on.

Attention metadata is built per microbatch and carried in the forward
contexts the threads install, not in the caller's.

FULL uses padded sizes; `for_capture` refreshes metadata from dummy block
tables. Eager steps split by the DP-agreed uniform token count in
`dp_sync_state` (see `create_ubatch_slices`); FULL replays the split its
graph captured with.

`UBatchState`                    *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils.UBatchState*

Bases: `NamedTuple`

Per-microbatch inputs for one dual-batch-overlap step.

                          *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils._slice_input_batch*
`_slice_input_batch(input_batch, ubatch_slice, query_start_loc_buf,
    seq_lens_buf, dcp_local_seq_lens_buf=None, *, dcp_size=1, dcp_rank=0,
    cp_interleave=1)`

Build the sub-`InputBatch` a single microbatch runs on.

A request straddling the boundary appears in both microbatches, its query
truncated to the tokens each one owns.

Query offsets and sequence lengths (including DCP-local lengths) are written
to the caller's persistent buffers after truncation. Other GPU inputs are
views of the full batch's buffers.

The sub-batch describes the forward pass only. Sampling runs once over the
merged batch, so `logits_indices`, `cu_num_logits` and the draft-token
fields are carried over unchanged and must not be read off a sub-batch.

                      *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils._slice_query_start_loc*
`_slice_query_start_loc(query_start_loc, out, req_start, req_stop,
    tok_start, num_tokens_padded)`

Rebase query_start_loc onto the microbatch's token range.

The clamp truncates the requests straddling either boundary to the tokens
this microbatch owns.

                             *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils._slice_seq_lens*
`_slice_seq_lens(seq_lens, out, query_start_loc, req_start, req_stop,
    tok_stop)`

Slice seq_lens, shortening the request truncated at the boundary.

Only tokens past the end of this microbatch are missing; tokens it owns in
an earlier microbatch are computed before this one reads them, so they still
count. Deriving the truncation from this microbatch's own query lengths
would subtract them twice. It is computed from tensors, not Python ints, so
this stays valid inside a CUDA graph.

                        *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils.create_ubatch_slices*
`create_ubatch_slices(input_batch, num_ubatches, uniform_token_count=None)`

Split a DP-padded batch into the slices its microbatches run on.

Splitting at the midpoint of the DP-padded token count leaves the trailing
microbatch anywhere from full to entirely inside the padding. Clamping its
request slice onto the last request leaves it holding that request with zero
query tokens -- the shape a straddling request already takes -- so it stays
well-formed with no work to do, like a dummy run.

A uniform batch of multi-token queries (spec decode verification) is split
on a request boundary instead, so each microbatch stays a uniform decode.
`uniform_token_count` must be agreed across DP ranks.

                   *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils.maybe_build_ubatch_runner*
`maybe_build_ubatch_runner(vllm_config, device, model_state, attn_groups,
    kv_cache_config, max_num_reqs)`

Build the microbatch runner, or None when DBO is not in use.

With more than one DP rank, the DP handshake agrees on each split. With one
DP rank, only `all-reduce-overlap` splits, as a local decision.

                        *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.ubatch_utils.merge_ubatch_outputs*
`merge_ubatch_outputs(outputs)`

Reassemble the full-batch model output from the per-microbatch ones.

Models return hidden states, a tuple of those plus a list of auxiliary
hidden states (EAGLE3, DFlash, DSpark), or IntermediateTensors on non-final
pipeline ranks.

                              *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.warmup._measure_sizing_step*
`_measure_sizing_step(model_runner)`

Record how far a sizing step grows torch's reservation from an emptied
cache, as serving starts once the cache is sized. Unlike the allocated peak,
this includes fragmentation, e.g. a large per-layer workspace that no longer
fits the segments freed around it. Allocations the step keeps are not
counted.

                             *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.warmup._reserved_block_count*
`_reserved_block_count(num_tokens, group, *, vllm_config,
    num_lookahead_tokens, max_model_len, max_encoder_len, dcp_world_size=1)`

Number of blocks the scheduler would hold for a request of `num_tokens`.

Warmup hand-builds its `SchedulerOutput`s, so it must reserve what
`KVCacheManager.allocate_slots` reserves: the token range plus
`num_lookahead_tokens`, where the speculator writes the KV of its drafts. A
DCP-sharded block holds `dcp_world_size` times its tokens.

                                         *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.warmup._run_step*
`_run_step(worker_execute_model, worker_sample_tokens, scheduler_output)`

Run one synthetic step and wait for the GPU to finish it.

UvaBufferPool reuses a staging slot two writes later, which is safe in
serving because the engine waits on each step's output. Warmup discards the
outputs, so without this a slow GPU reads slots already overwritten.

                             *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.warmup._warmup_block_counter*

Bind `_reserved_block_count` to `model_runner`'s reservation policy.

                                 *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.warmup._warmup_token_ids*

                        *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.warmup.run_context_prefill_warmup*
`run_context_prefill_warmup(model_runner, worker_execute_model,
    worker_sample_tokens, num_context_tokens)`

Run a prefill step over about `num_context_tokens` of cached context.

MLA up-projects a prefix cache hit's context chunk by chunk, a transient
that no step starting from an empty prefix reaches. The queries are kept
short: the full-budget step already measured theirs.

                        *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.warmup.run_kv_cache_sizing_warmup*

                   *vllm.v1.worker.gpu.warmup.run_mixed_prefill_decode_warmup*

`maybe_rocm_profiling_fallback(profile_result)`

Memory in bytes to size the KV cache from when profiling measured a release
on ROCm, or None to keep what profiling measured.

The measurement is the drop in free device memory across startup, so it
comes out negative when anything else on the device released memory
meanwhile. Torch reserved is process local, so it stands in as a lower bound
instead of refusing to start. Kept to ROCm, where the AMD CI groups hit
this, following #45490.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                             *vllm.v1.worker.iteration_timing*

Non-blocking GPU timing of engine iterations.

An iteration is timed between two CUDA events recorded on the output
worker's stream: one before `execute_model`, one after `sample_tokens`
returns. The interval covers the model forward pass, sampling and
speculative drafting, including host submission gaps.

The end event is often still pending when the iteration's own output is
built, so a finished timing leaves the worker as a record with the first
reply built after its end event has completed: the iteration's own output, a
later step's output or a dummy batch. No step waits for a timing, so the
last iterations before the engine goes idle are reported once it steps
again.

                        *vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils.MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext*
`MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext` `dataclass`

Context for GPU-side Mamba state copy operations during the fused
postprocess path.

Used for hybrid speculative state maintenance and for model-owned ReplaySSM
tracker prefix-cache lifecycle maintenance.

Precomputes memory layout metadata (base addresses, strides, element sizes)
so the GPU kernel can perform state copies without CPU-GPU sync.

State types are distinguished by conv_width: >0 for conv states (sliding
window with offset-based copies), 0 for temporal states (full block copies).

  physical state IDs in one launch.
- `create` -- Create context with allocated buffers (metadata populated
  later).
- `initialize_from_forward_context` -- Extract and cache memory layout
  metadata from Mamba state tensors.
- `run_fused_postprocess_align` -- V2 align postprocess: save the running
  state to the block-aligned
- `run_fused_precopy` -- Pre-copy each request's previous running block into
  its new window

*vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils.MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext.compute_aligned_state_indices*
`compute_aligned_state_indices(seq_lens, num_reqs)`

Compute every Mamba group's aligned physical state IDs in one launch.

                 *vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils.MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext.create*
`create(max_num_reqs, kv_cache_config, copy_funcs, forward_context, device)`
`classmethod`

Create context with allocated buffers (metadata populated later).

*vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils.MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext.initialize_from_forward_context*
`initialize_from_forward_context(kv_cache_config, forward_context,
    mamba_state_copy_funcs, block_tables, aligned_index_block_tables=None)`

Extract and cache memory layout metadata from Mamba state tensors.

This method populates the pre-allocated metadata tensors with information
needed by `postprocess_mamba_fused_kernel` to perform state copies entirely
on the GPU without CPU-GPU synchronization.

For each Mamba layer and state type, the following metadata is extracted: -
state_base_addrs: GPU memory address (data_ptr) of the state tensor -
state_block_strides: Bytes between consecutive blocks (stride * elem_size) -
state_elem_sizes: Element size in bytes (e.g., 2 for float16) -
state_inner_sizes: For conv states, elements per conv position (stride(1)),
used to compute offset when slicing state[block, offset:]. For temporal
states, this field is unused (set to 1). - state_conv_widths: Conv dimension
size for conv states, 0 for temporal states

The conv vs temporal state type is detected by inspecting the copy function
name: functions containing "conv" are treated as conv states.

This method is idempotent - it only executes once (guarded by is_initialized
flag) since the metadata is static after model loading.

Parameters: ~

- `kv_cache_config` (KVCacheConfig) -- Configuration containing KV cache
  group info and layer name mappings.
- `forward_context` (dict[str, Any]) -- Dictionary mapping layer names to
  attention objects, populated after the model is loaded. Each attention
  object must have a kv_cache attribute containing the list of state
  tensors.
- `mamba_state_copy_funcs` (MambaStateCopyFuncsByType) -- Mapping from
  MambaAttentionBackendEnum to copy functions.
- `block_tables` (list[Tensor]) -- per-mamba-group persistent block-table
  tensors, in the same order as mamba_group_ids, with one row per request
  state slot. Their data_ptr() / stride(0) are captured once for the
  state-copy kernels to index into.
- `aligned_index_block_tables` (list[Tensor] | None, default: None ) --
  per-mamba-group persistent tables read by compute_aligned_state_indices,
  with one row per batch row. Defaults to block_tables.

*vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils.MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext.run_fused_postprocess_align*
`run_fused_postprocess_align(num_reqs, num_accepted_tokens_gpu,
    state_idx_gpu, new_num_computed_tokens_gpu, idx_mapping)`

V2 align postprocess: save the running state to the block-aligned position
after spec-decode acceptance leaves the sequence non-aligned.

`num_accepted_tokens_gpu` is updated in place while the kernel reads from a
snapshot to avoid cross-program races when the accepted position stays in
the running block and the count is reset to 1. `new_num_computed_tokens`
already holds the post-step computed count (PRECOMPUTED_NEW_COMPUTED).
`idx_mapping` maps batch row -> req-state slot (HAS_IDX_MAPPING).

      *vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils.MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext.run_fused_precopy*
`run_fused_precopy(num_reqs, state_idx_gpu, src_col_gpu, token_bias_gpu,
    idx_mapping)`

Pre-copy each request's previous running block into its new window block
before the forward pass (align boundary migration).

Parameters: ~

- `num_reqs` (int) -- Number of active requests (batch order).
- `state_idx_gpu` (Tensor) -- [max_reqs] post-advance dst block column per
  req slot.
- `src_col_gpu` (Tensor) -- [max_reqs] pre-advance src block column (-1 =
  fresh).
- `token_bias_gpu` (Tensor) -- [max_reqs] accepted-token bias (num_accepted
  - 1).

- `idx_mapping` (Tensor | None) -- optional [num_reqs] batch_idx ->
  req_state_idx. None means batch order already equals request state order.

                          *vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils._copy_mamba_state_block*
`_copy_mamba_state_block(state_idx, bt_row_idx, src_col, dst_col,
    token_bias, block_table_ptrs_ptr, block_table_stride_req,
    state_base_addrs_ptr, state_block_strides_ptr, state_elem_sizes_ptr,
    state_inner_sizes_ptr, state_conv_widths_ptr, state_group_indices_ptr,
    state_dim_row_count_ptr, state_dim_row_stride_ptr, tile_idx,
    COPY_BLOCK_SIZE, CONV_STATE_DIM_FIRST, TEMPORAL_TILES)`

Copy one (layer, state-type) mamba state block between block columns.

Shared copy body of `postprocess_mamba_fused_kernel` and
`precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel`: - conv state (conv_width > 0): shift the
window by `token_bias` tokens,
`state[bt[src_col], token_bias:] -> state[bt[dst_col], :conv_width - token_bias]`
- temporal state: `token_bias` selects the accepted speculative column,
`state[bt[src_col + token_bias]] -> state[bt[dst_col]]`

The caller owns the decision logic (which columns, whether to copy); this
device function only performs the byte copy for the given metadata slot.

`tile_idx` in `[0, TEMPORAL_TILES)` partitions the temporal state's u64
range into `TEMPORAL_TILES` contiguous, COPY_BLOCK_SIZE-aligned slices,
giving more CTAs to fill the SMs at small batch (multi-MiB temporal copies
otherwise leave the GPU under-filled). Conv states are small; only
`tile_idx == 0` copies them. `TEMPORAL_TILES == 1` and `tile_idx == 0`
reproduces the untiled behavior.

                                *vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils._memcpy_u64_tiled*
`_memcpy_u64_tiled(src_addr, dst_addr, copy_size, tile_idx, COPY_BLOCK_SIZE,
    NUM_TILES)`

Head/body/tail memcpy with the u64 body split across `NUM_TILES` CTAs.

Fast path (`src` and `dst` share sub-8B alignment): tile 0 owns the byte
head that lifts dst to 8B and the 0-7 byte tail; body tiles vectorize as u64
over the aligned interior. `NUM_TILES=1` collapses to a single- CTA memcpy.
Production callers derive both addresses from the same
`state_base_addr + block_id * stride` and always take this path.

Slow path (mismatched sub-8B alignment): byte-wide tiled copy. Some NVIDIA
parts (e.g. GB200) reject misaligned u64 loads with
`cudaErrorMisalignedAddress` instead of accepting the misaligned-sector
cost, so we can't just let the fast path run with a misaligned src.

                              *vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils.get_mamba_group_ids*
`get_mamba_group_ids(mamba_groups)`

A group whose layers use different `MambaSpec`s is listed under one key per
spec, so the same group id can appear more than once.

                   *vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils.postprocess_mamba_fused_kernel*
`postprocess_mamba_fused_kernel(num_accepted_tokens_ptr,
    mamba_state_idx_ptr, num_scheduled_tokens_ptr, num_computed_tokens_ptr,
    num_draft_tokens_ptr, block_table_ptrs_ptr, block_table_stride_req,
    state_base_addrs_ptr, state_block_strides_ptr, state_elem_sizes_ptr,
    state_inner_sizes_ptr, state_conv_widths_ptr, state_group_indices_ptr,
    state_dim_row_count_ptr, state_dim_row_stride_ptr,
    num_accepted_tokens_out_ptr, idx_mapping_ptr, num_reqs, block_size,
    COPY_BLOCK_SIZE, CONV_STATE_DIM_FIRST, HAS_IDX_MAPPING=False,
    PRECOMPUTED_NEW_COMPUTED=False, SKIP_TEMPORAL_STATE_COPY=False,
    TEMPORAL_TILES=1)`

Fused GPU kernel for postprocess_mamba that computes decisions AND performs
mamba state copies without any CPU-GPU synchronization.

Grid: (num_reqs, num_states [, TEMPORAL_TILES]) - program_id(0) =
request/batch index - program_id(1) = state_idx (flattened index into
layer/state_type metadata) - program_id(2) = temporal-copy tile index (0
when TEMPORAL_TILES == 1)

The kernel indexes directly into pre-flattened metadata arrays using
program_id(1). The grid dimensions encode the total state count.

                 *vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils.precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel*
`precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel(mamba_state_idx_ptr, src_col_ptr,
    token_bias_ptr, block_table_ptrs_ptr, block_table_stride_req,
    state_base_addrs_ptr, state_block_strides_ptr, state_elem_sizes_ptr,
    state_inner_sizes_ptr, state_conv_widths_ptr, state_group_indices_ptr,
    state_dim_row_count_ptr, state_dim_row_stride_ptr, idx_mapping_ptr,
    num_reqs, COPY_BLOCK_SIZE, CONV_STATE_DIM_FIRST, HAS_IDX_MAPPING=True,
    ZERO_TEMPORAL_TOKEN_BIAS=False, TEMPORAL_TILES=1)`

Pre-copy mamba state across block boundaries.

Before the forward pass, copy each request's last SSM/conv state from its
previous block column into the new window block column, so the kernels read
the initial state from the write-side block as usual. Same per-(layer,
state) copy semantics as `postprocess_mamba_fused_kernel` (shared
`_copy_mamba_state_block` body), but driven by the GPU-resident src columns
so it needs no CPU-GPU sync (async-scheduling safe).

Grid: (num_reqs, num_states [, TEMPORAL_TILES]). The runner passes a
batch-to-state idx_mapping; HAS_IDX_MAPPING=False is for arrays already
staged in batch order.

              *vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils.preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel*
`preprocess_mamba_align_fused_kernel(idx_mapping_ptr, state_idx_ptr,
    num_computed_tokens_ptr, query_start_loc_ptr, num_accepted_tokens_ptr,
    src_col_ptr, src_off_ptr, num_reqs, BLOCK_SIZE, MAMBA_BLOCK_SIZE,
    HAS_IDX_MAPPING=True)`

Fused align preprocess: emit the pre-copy src column/offset AND advance
state_idx in a single launch (V2 align).

Per batch_idx (0..num_reqs-1), resolving req slot via idx_mapping: 1. Read
pre-advance state_idx and num_accepted (last step's values). 2. Store the
pre-copy src columns for `precopy_mamba_align_fused_kernel`: - src_col =
state_idx (the previous running block column) - src_off = max(num_accepted -
1, 0) (the accepted-token bias) 3. Advance state_idx to the new running
block. Reset num_accepted to 1 when the block changes: the migrated
convolution state now sits at the start of the new block and must be read
with the neutral accepted-token bias. ReplaySSM ring cursors are migrated
separately.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                                 *vllm.v1.worker.startup_plan*

Persist and reuse the memory-profiling result across engine boots.

On startup, vLLM measures how much GPU memory the KV cache can use and
computes the `--kv-cache-memory` value that reproduces that allocation. For
a fixed (model, config, hardware, library) combination the result is
deterministic, yet it is re-measured on every boot.

When `VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1`, each worker persists that value under
`{VLLM_CACHE_ROOT}/startup_plan/` (regenerable derived state, alongside the
torch.compile cache), keyed by a fingerprint of everything the value depends
on, and later boots apply it automatically -- skipping the memory-profiling
measurement and the CUDA-graph memory estimation pass -- if and only if the
fingerprint matches and the device has at least as much free memory as when
the plan was recorded. On any mismatch the worker falls back to full
profiling, so a stale plan costs nothing and is never trusted.

Functions: ~

- `compute_plan_fingerprint` -- Hash everything the profiled KV-cache memory
  value depends on.
- `maybe_apply_startup_plan` -- If enabled and --kv-cache-memory was not set
  explicitly, apply a
- `maybe_save_startup_plan` -- Atomically persist this boot's profiling
  result for future boots.

               *vllm.v1.worker.startup_plan._applicable_kv_cache_memory_bytes*
`_applicable_kv_cache_memory_bytes(plan, current_free_memory)`

The apply-time OOM-safety gate.

The recorded value is only valid if the device has at least as much free
memory now as when the plan was measured (co-tenants, leaked allocations, or
MIG changes all reduce it). Outside that envelope, return None and let the
caller re-profile.

`_plan_path(fingerprint)`             *vllm.v1.worker.startup_plan._plan_path*

cache root (like the torch.compile cache) and relocate with
`VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` instead of needing a location knob of their own.

                        *vllm.v1.worker.startup_plan.compute_plan_fingerprint*
`compute_plan_fingerprint(vllm_config, rank, world_size,
    pp_transport='nccl')`

Hash everything the profiled KV-cache memory value depends on.

`VllmConfig.compile_factors()` covers the vLLM version and the model, cache,
parallel, and compilation configs, but deliberately contains no device
identity (`DeviceConfig.compile_factors` is empty), so device name, total
memory, compute capability, and the torch/CUDA build are added here. The
vLLM version is also pinned as an explicit factor so version invalidation
holds no matter how `compile_factors` evolves. Rank is included because
per-rank memory use differs under TP/PP. Driver-only changes are not part of
the key; the free-memory gate at apply time bounds the residual risk.

                        *vllm.v1.worker.startup_plan.maybe_apply_startup_plan*

`VLLM_ENABLE_STARTUP_PLAN=1`.
